about: Klartext: the feed unit is carried by the word (FU, FZ) and a plain F ends it; a cycle definition runs over its `~` parameter list, runs nothing itself, and stays defined for every call after it (M9, WP9.5b: the defined cycle of plan 7.4, which changed the claims on lines 7, 10, 16, 17, 34, 37 and 40).

states.about: `BEGIN PGM … MM` says which units the program is written in, so the units are no longer assumed from line 1 on.
A tool call carries the tool, the speed and a feed in one block.
The cycle definition stores the cycle and runs nothing: no cycle in the block, none active (plan 7.4 rule 1).
A `~` continuation is the same block: still a definition, still nothing that runs.
The last parameter line of the block.
M99 runs the defined cycle once at this position; its F is no lead, and nothing stays active (plan 7.4 rule 3).
A tool call without a feed leaves the feed where it was.
Rigid tapping: the definition replaces the drilling cycle; the pitch is its parameter Q239, so no feed word of a block is a lead.
The thread-pitch parameter line, still inside the same block.
M99 runs the tap: the cycle of this block is the defined one, its F would still be a positioning feed.
`FZ0.05` on the tool call: the feed of this program is per tooth from here on.
`FMAX` is not a feed word, so the unit is unchanged.
A plain F ends the per-tooth mode; a Q parameter as its value is remembered as written and marked.
The reset the goldens are here for: after `FU`, a plain `F800` is no longer per revolution.
